thread:
Evan (Support): Heads up — customer NimbusPay hit a hard throughput drop + spike in 5xx during their morning ramp at ~08:22 UTC. They reported ~9% 503s and lots of client retries.
Maya (Sales): NimbusPay is on a paid pilot w/ a latency SLA. They're escalated and want a mitigation plan. Looping @Rashmi (PM).
Rashmi (PM): Thanks. Evan, paste route, model, region, concurrency and any sample payloads. Also did they see this immediately after a deploy?
Evan (Support): Route: /v1/generate (nimbuspay-prod). Model: redwood/gpt-max-quant. Seq ~580, client concurrency ~170 from multiple IPs in eu-west-1. Repro snippet: 
```
POST /v1/generate
{"model":"redwood/gpt-max-quant","input":"<~450 tokens>"}
=> 503 {"error":"instance overload"}
```
Tomas (Eng): Telemetry: significant pod restarts in eu-west-1 pool-7 at ~08:20. I see GPU OOMs then kube OOMKills and subsequent scheduler retries. We rolled v2026.09.25.08.15 to that pool — included a kernel scheduling tweak for large KV caching. Hypothesis: mem residency spikes on certain KV paths under high concurrency.
Anya (Oncall): Confirmed OOM events and ingress queue buildup. Nginx p95 spiked; autoscaler kept spinning up nodes but pods failed before healthy.
deploybot: Deploy v2026.09.25.08.15 -> pool-7 completed at 2026-09-25T08:15:00Z
Maya (Sales): Customer timeline matches that deploy. NimbusPay asked for either immediate fallback to a known-good variant or a rollback. Prefer non-disruptive first.
Rashmi (PM): Triage options: (1) Per-route fallback to `redwood/gpt-max-fp16` (low risk, small output delta). (2) Route NimbusPay to a dedicated EU capacity (good perf, provisioning ~40min). (3) Full rollback of scheduling tweak (higher blast radius, ~1h). What do we have capacity-wise?
Tomas (Eng): Dedicated EU capacity has some headroom in eu-west-2 but not eu-west-1; cross-region will add latency. Fallback is fastest. Also we can add an automatic routing policy to prefer fp16 when mem pressure triggers.
Anya (Oncall): I'll stand up alerting: `nimbuspay_error_rate > 2% for 1m` pages eng-oncall. Also watching node OOMs and pod restart counters.
Evan (Support): NimbusPay prefers a quick fallback + a short canary. They want to sample outputs before a full flip.
Rashmi (PM): OK decision: perform (1) fallback canary 50 requests at 10% traffic, measure p95+errors for 15m. If stable, promote to 100% and monitor for 3 hours. Action owners: Tomas -> apply route override + logs, Anya -> infra watch/paging, Evan -> coordinate with Nimbus, Maya -> customer comms and SLA note.
Tomas (Eng): Applying override now: `PATCH /v1/routes/nimbuspay-prod` body: `{ "model_override": "redwood/gpt-max-fp16", "canary_requests": 50, "canary_pct": 10 }`
Anya (Oncall): Watch dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/kvcache/nimbuspay?from=2334567800&to=2334568600. Temporary pager rule in place.
Evan (Support): Canary results: 50 requests routed; NimbusPay reports p95 ~290ms and error rate 0.8% (down from ~9%). They want a 3-hour stability window after full switch and a postmortem.
Maya (Sales): Noted. I've messaged NimbusPay: we've started a fallback canary, will promote if stable, hourly updates for 3h, and a formal RCA/timeline in 72h. They've asked finance/legal to be notified about SLA exposure.
Rashmi (PM): Backlog items (owners/due dates):
- P0 RCA (Tomas): Repro mem spike with scheduling tweak + high concurrency. Due 72h. Acceptance: reproducible test in staging + targeted fix or config gate + regression benchmark.
- P1 Product: Per-route auto-fallback spec (Rashmi). Due 2 sprints. Acceptance: product doc + API proposal + ops playbook.
- P1 Ops: Rollback playbook and customer mitigation checklist (Anya). Due 5 days. Acceptance: tested runbook and communication templates.
- P2 SLA calc & comms (Maya): Due 24h. Acceptance: customer credit calc + status email template.
Tomas (Eng): Created ticket NIM-1202 and uploaded logs, heapdumps, and a staging reproducer plan. Will keep the override for 3h then reassess.
deploybot: NIM-1202 created by tomas (Eng)
Rashmi (PM): Customer-facing acceptance criteria to close:
- NimbusPay p95 < 400ms and error rate < 1% for continuous 3h
- RCA delivered and patch scheduled for canary with no regression
- Product spec for auto-fallback added and prioritized on roadmap
Evan (Support): I'll follow up with NimbusPay in 1 hour and update thread.
Anya (Oncall): If error rate > 2% I'll escalate and propose spinning up dedicated eu-west-2 capacity as a temporary move. Rota on standby.
Maya (Sales): Sending hourly status to NimbusPay now. Also flagged SLA risk with finance/legal.
Tomas (Eng): Canary looks good; promoting to 100% now. Streaming heapdumps to NIM-1202.
Evan (Support): NimbusPay confirms 100% routed; p95 ~330ms, errors 0.5%. They requested hourly updates and a postmortem.
Rashmi (PM): Thanks all. We'll track NIM-1202 and the product epic for auto-fallback. If fallback fails we'll escalate to dedicated routing or rollback. :white_check_mark:
